speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand your infant is presenting with bilious vomiting, an inability to pass meconium, and abdominal distension. To determine the cause, have you noticed any specific shapes of the stool or any family history of bowel obstructions?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung's disease. The combination of bilious vomiting, failure to pass meconium within 48 hours, and abdominal distension in a newborn is highly suggestive of intestinal obstruction due to aganglionosis. We will proceed with a rectal exam and abdominal X-ray to confirm.
